messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1767777776 — Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed targeting /v1/generate. Auto-paging sanjay (oncall).

incident-bot: Severity: P1 | Start: 2026-02-28T15:02:56Z | Symptom: 5xx spike + tail latency timeouts > 5s | Affected: hosted inference region eu-west-1 | Runbook: batching/scheduler saturation

sanjay (oncall): saw alerts from grafana and datadog. 5xx jump at 15:02, error rate ~12% for last 3m. Some 504s at the gateway.

elaine (sre): confirming — traces show long queue wait times in scheduler, head-of-line blocking. KV-cache miss rate spiked. Looks like one old model replica started producing huge KV load and slowed down batching.

kevin (prod-eng): which model? can we route away?

elaine (sre): model: open-redwood/phi-13b-v1 (eu-west-1 pool). One replica reporting CPU+mem thrash and huge token-increment latency. Batcher queue length per shard: 220 -> saturation.

todd (eng-runtime): taking a look at scheduler logs now. Running `kubectl logs -n runtime scheduler-pt-3 -f` and grepping for queue metrics.

todd (eng-runtime): found repeated warnings: `batcher: queue_delay > 2000ms, hol_block=true, inflight_batches=8` and then `gateway: upstream timeout` a few seconds later.

elaine (sre): impact: customer-facing APIs degrade; embedding requests less affected. Severity confirmed P1. jess — any customer reports?

jess (support): Support hub: two enterprise seats opened cases, one reporting 30% failures from eu-west-1 between 15:02-15:06. Noticed retries causing request bursts.

sanjay (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily scale down model weight to remove the slow replica; 2) enable routing fallback to phi-7b-quant for non-enterprise; 3) increase max batch size throttle to reduce HOL blocking; 4) apply short-term request shedding on gateway for bursty clients.

todd (eng-runtime): ACTION: triggering drain on the problematic replica and draining scheduler connections to it. Command:```bash
# mark node unschedulable for model pool
redctl pool set-state eu-west-phi-13b-v1 replica-7 drain
```

todd (eng-runtime): also pushing a temporary routing rule to route new requests to phi-7b-quant when queue_wait > 1200ms:```yaml
- match: route:/v1/generate
  when:
    queue_wait_ms: ">1200"
  route_to: model:open-redwood/phi-7b-quant
```

elaine (sre): enabling gateway short-circuit: drop non-critical long-poll requests older than 6s and return 503 with Retry-After. Might reduce retry storm.

kevin (prod-eng): can we do a selective canary rollback of the model version? that replica started after a rollout ~2h ago.

todd (eng-runtime): yes — rollback to phi-13b-v1@rev-20260228-01 for pool eu-west-1. Doing canary rollback on 2 nodes then scale up. Command:```bash
redctl model rollback open-redwood/phi-13b-v1 rev-20260228-01 --pool eu-west-phi-13b-v1 --nodes 2
```

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled in 30m. Pager duty escalation disabled while mitigation in progress.

elaine (sre): I'm watching tail latencies and the batcher queue heatmap. After drain command, queue length per shard fell from 220 -> 60 in ~45s. Error rate dropped to ~4% at 15:05.

jess (support): customers reporting partial recovery, some still seeing intermittent 502/504s. Raising comms to status page: draft message: "We are investigating increased error rates in eu-west-1 for text generation endpoints; mitigation in progress."

kevin (prod-eng): note: KV-cache warmed entries were evicted during the slow replica's behavior, causing some cold-KV slowdown for a while; we'll see a secondary latency bump as caches warm back up.

sanjay (oncall): follow-up items: 1) keep rollback until we confirm stable metrics for 30m; 2) run a targeted eval of throughput on phi-13b-v1 staging to reproduce cache pressure; 3) add a scheduler guard to preempt batches if queue_wait > 2500ms to avoid HOL.

todd (eng-runtime): added temporary guard:```python
# reject-long-wait.py (temporary)
def should_preempt(batch):
    return batch.queue_wait_ms > 2500
```

applied to runtime v2.3-canary.

elaine (sre): metrics at 15:12: error rate steady ~0.8%, p95 latency dropping to normal. Holding incident at P2 for now while we monitor.

jess (support): status page message published and customers notified. Sent targeted note to the two enterprise contacts with current remediation steps.

sanjay (oncall): postmortem checklist: collect scheduler traces, model rollout timeline, replica logs, KV-cache eviction events, and gateway retry logs. Assign owners: todd for runtime logs, elaine for metrics/dashboards, jess for customer comms.

kevin (prod-eng): long-term: implement smarter model rollout gate that verifies KV/memory growth thresholds before increasing replica count; add per-replica circuit-breaker at router.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1767777776 updated: Status: mitigated -> monitoring. Final note: root cause suspected partial model rollout causing KV cache thrash and head-of-line saturation in batching layer.

sanjay (oncall): handing off to elaine at 15:30 for monitoring window. If error rate creeps >2% for 5m, re-open P1 and page.

elaine (sre): ack. collecting all artifacts now. will file postmortem with timeline and runbook updates.

jess (support): closing customer-facing loop after 1h with follow-up summary.

kevin (prod-eng): thumbs up.

sanjay (oncall): leaving short notes in the incident doc: `root_cause_hypothesis: rollout -> single replica KV thrash -> scheduler HOL -> gateway timeouts`

elaine (sre): final metrics snapshot: total requests during window: 1.3M, error count peak: 156k (12%), affected routes: /v1/generate primarily, median recovery time: 8m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1767777776 resolved->monitoring.
